# UIAO Document Index

This page provides a unified, searchable inventory of every customer-facing document
in the UIAO documentation corpus. All documents trace provenance to canonical sources
in the governance repository.

## How to Use This Index

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Family** | Document family (executive-briefs, adapter-specs, etc.) |
| **Pillar** | Taxonomy pillar (Modernization, Compliance, Substrate) |
| **Title** | Document title as rendered on the site |
| **Status** | `Active`, `Stub`, or other frontmatter status |
| **Audience** | Primary intended readership |

::: {.callout-note}
The **Document Families** and **Pillar Taxonomy** tables below are
regenerated from `docs/customer-documents/**` on every build by
[`scripts/generate_document_index.py`](../../scripts/generate_document_index.py).
Status, Audience, and Title columns reflect each file's actual
frontmatter; sub-category Status defers to whether the directory
contains authored sibling content. Drift is blocked in CI by the
`document-index-status` workflow.
:::

## Canon Invariants

All documents in this index are governed by the following invariants:

1. **GCC-Moderate boundary** — all content scoped to Commercial Cloud / GCC-Moderate
2. **Commercial Cloud** — Amazon Connect Contact Center is the only non-GCC exception
3. **No FOUO markings** — use "Controlled" classification until agency adoption
4. **Single Source of Truth** — every document traces provenance to `canon/`
5. **No former-repo references** — all paths reference the unified `uiao` monorepo

---

::: {.callout-tip}
## Keeping This Index Current
The tables above are regenerated from the tree — never hand-edit them.
To refresh after adding, renaming, or removing customer-documents:

```bash
python scripts/generate_document_index.py \
    --output docs/data/document-index-tables.md
```

The `document-index-status` CI workflow re-runs the generator on every
PR that touches `docs/customer-documents/**` and fails if the committed
`docs/data/document-index-tables.md` does not match the regenerated
output. Run the command above locally and commit the refreshed file
to resolve a failing run.
:::
